steps.heading: Add stock
steps.description: Pour in the meat stock gradually, breaking the egusi into lumps.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Add crayfish, pepper, iru and dried fish and simmer until the oil rises.

steps.heading: Greens
steps.description: Stir in the washed bitter leaf and cook two minutes more.

name: Vegetable Sauce
whatMakesItGood: Cut everything the same size and cook it fast on high heat. Vegetables stewed slowly go grey and watery.
description: A quick sauce of carrot, cabbage, green beans and pepper for yam, rice or plantain.

steps.heading: Prep
steps.description: Slice all the vegetables to a similar size so they cook evenly.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Fry the onion, blended pepper and tomato in oil until thick.

steps.heading: Add vegetables
steps.description: Stir the vegetables in on high heat and keep them moving.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Season and take it off while they still have bite.

name: Adalu (Beans and Corn)
whatMakesItGood: Corn takes longer than beans, so it goes in first. Added together, the beans turn to paste before the corn is anywhere near done.
description: Beans and corn cooked together until both are soft, finished with palm oil and pepper.

steps.heading: Start the corn
steps.description: Soak the corn, then boil it on its own until it begins to soften.

steps.heading: Add the beans
steps.description: Add the beans and keep cooking, topping up with hot water as needed.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Once both are soft, stir in palm oil, blended pepper, onion, crayfish and stock cubes.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Simmer together, mash a little for body, and salt to taste.

name: Dundu and Pepper Sauce
whatMakesItGood: Soak the cut yam in salted water before frying — it seasons it through and stops the pieces sticking together in the oil.
description: Fried yam chips with a rough, oily pepper sauce for dipping.

steps.heading: Prepare the yam
steps.description: Peel and cut into thick chips, then soak in salted water for ten minutes.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Drain and dry the yam, then fry in hot oil until golden and crisp at the edges.

steps.heading: Make the sauce
steps.description: Blend the peppers and onion roughly and fry in palm oil with the stock cubes until thick.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Salt the yam while hot and serve with the sauce.

name: Moin Moin
whatMakesItGood: The batter must be loose enough to pour but not watery. Too thick and it steams into a brick; too thin and it never sets.
description: Steamed bean pudding with pepper, onion and whatever you fold in — egg, fish or corned beef.

steps.heading: Peel the beans
steps.description: Soak and rub off every skin, then rinse clean.

steps.heading: Blend
steps.description: Blend with the peppers and onion into a smooth batter, using as little water as you can.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Stir in the oil, stock cubes and salt until fully combined and slightly loose.

steps.heading: Fill
steps.description: Pour into leaves, tins or bowls, adding egg or sardine to each.

steps.heading: Steam
steps.description: Steam over medium heat until firm and a knife comes out clean.

name: Ewa Agoyin Sauce
whatMakesItGood: The colour comes from cooking the onions and pepper far past where you would normally stop. It should look almost burnt, and taste sweet rather than sharp.
description: Very dark, very oily pepper sauce cooked down slowly — the black sauce that goes over mashed beans.

steps.heading: Blend the onions
steps.description: Blend the onions coarsely — they are the body of the sauce, not a background note.

steps.heading: Heat the oil
steps.description: Heat the palm oil until very hot, then lower the flame.

steps.heading: Fry long
steps.description: Add the onions and fry patiently until they darken well past golden.

steps.heading: Add pepper
steps.description: Stir in the dry pepper and stock cubes and keep cooking until the sauce is almost black and the oil has separated.

steps.heading: Rest
steps.description: Take it off and let it settle before serving over mashed beans.

name: Nigerian Fried Rice
whatMakesItGood: The colour is curry, not turmeric, and the rice is parboiled in seasoned stock so the flavour is inside the grain rather than sitting on it.
description: Rice fried with liver, curry and diced vegetables — green and yellow rather than red.

steps.heading: Make the stock
steps.description: Boil the liver with onion, curry, thyme and stock cubes, then dice it and keep the stock.

steps.heading: Parboil the rice
steps.description: Parboil the rice in the seasoned stock so it takes the colour and flavour, then drain and cool.

steps.heading: Fry the vegetables
steps.description: Fry the diced carrots, beans and peas briefly on high heat so they stay firm.

steps.heading: Combine
steps.description: Add the rice and liver and toss on high heat until everything is coated and hot through.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Check the seasoning and serve.

name: Jollof Spaghetti
whatMakesItGood: Break the spaghetti in half and cook it in the sauce. Boiling it separately and mixing gives you pasta with stew, which is a different dish.
description: Spaghetti cooked in the stew base until it takes the colour — quicker than rice and just as filling.

steps.heading: Build the base
steps.description: Blend and reduce the peppers and tomato, then fry in oil with the paste until the oil separates.

steps.heading: Season the liquid
steps.description: Add curry, thyme, stock cubes and just enough water to cook the pasta.

steps.heading: Cook
steps.description: Break the spaghetti in, cover, and cook on low until the liquid is absorbed.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Stir once, check the salt, and serve.

name: Ofada Rice
whatMakesItGood: Ofada must be washed several times and parboiled with a change of water, or the strong smell overwhelms whatever you serve with it.
description: Unpolished local rice, boiled plain and served with ayamase — earthy and a little chewy.

steps.heading: Wash well
steps.description: Rinse the rice repeatedly until the water runs much clearer.

steps.heading: Parboil
steps.description: Boil for ten minutes, then throw that water away completely.

steps.heading: Cook
steps.description: Return to the pot with fresh salted water and cook until tender.

steps.heading: Steam
steps.description: Drain, cover, and let it steam off the heat for five minutes.

name: Agege Bread and Stew
whatMakesItGood: It exists because there is always stew left over. Warm the stew properly so the oil loosens and soaks into the bread.
description: Soft sweet bread torn and dipped into leftover stew — breakfast when there is stew in the fridge.

steps.heading: Make a quick stew
steps.description: Blend and fry the tomato, pepper and onion in oil until thick and the oil separates.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Add the stock cube and salt and simmer briefly.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Tear the bread and serve alongside for dipping.

name: Akara Osu
whatMakesItGood: Palm oil changes it completely: heavier, redder, and better with pap than the ordinary version.
description: Bean cakes fried in palm oil rather than vegetable oil — darker, denser and traditionally shaped flat.

steps.heading: Peel and blend
steps.description: Soak, peel and blend the beans thick with onion and pepper.

steps.heading: Whisk
steps.description: Beat the batter until it lightens and holds air.

steps.heading: Heat the oil
steps.description: Heat the palm oil until it is hot but not smoking.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Drop flattened spoonfuls in and fry until deep red-brown on both sides.

name: Okpa
whatMakesItGood: Okpa flour needs more water than it looks like it should, and palm oil is what makes it yellow rather than beige. Steam it hard or it stays wet in the middle.
description: Bambara nut pudding steamed in leaves — the Enugu breakfast, firm and deep yellow.

steps.heading: Mix the oil in
steps.description: Whisk the palm oil into the flour first, so the colour goes through evenly.

steps.heading: Add water
steps.description: Add warm water gradually to a smooth, pourable batter with no lumps.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Stir in the ground pepper, onion, stock cubes and salt.

steps.heading: Wrap
steps.description: Pour into leaves, foil or bowls and seal them.

steps.heading: Steam
steps.description: Steam for at least thirty-five minutes until fully set and firm.

name: Garri Soakings
whatMakesItGood: It exists because it needs nothing but water. Ijebu garri is the right one; it is sour and stays crunchy instead of turning to paste.
description: Garri soaked in cold water with sugar, groundnuts and milk — the meal that needs no fire.

steps.heading: Soak
steps.description: Put the garri in a bowl and pour cold water over it. Let it swell for a minute.

steps.heading: Sweeten
steps.description: Add sugar and milk and stir once.

steps.heading: Top
steps.description: Scatter the groundnuts over and eat straight away, before it softens.

name: Chicken Suya
whatMakesItGood: Chicken dries out faster than beef, so it needs a shorter, hotter grill. The second dusting of yaji after cooking is where the flavour lives.
description: Chicken strips in yaji, grilled hot and fast and dusted again off the heat.

steps.heading: Make the yaji
steps.description: Grind the groundnuts coarse and mix with dry pepper, ginger, stock cubes and salt.

steps.heading: Slice and coat
steps.description: Cut the chicken into thin strips, toss in oil, then in half the yaji.

steps.heading: Rest
steps.description: Let it sit so the spice takes.

steps.heading: Grill
steps.description: Grill hot and fast, turning once, until just cooked through.

steps.heading: Dust
steps.description: Dust with the remaining yaji and serve with raw onion.

name: Plantain Porridge
whatMakesItGood: Use unripe plantain — ripe turns sweet and falls apart. Some pieces should break down to thicken it, so cut them unevenly.
description: Unripe plantain simmered into a thick pottage with palm oil, pepper and greens.

steps.heading: Prepare
steps.description: Peel and cut the plantain into rough chunks of different sizes.

steps.heading: Boil
steps.description: Cook with the blended pepper, onion and tomato in just enough water to cover.

steps.heading: Enrich
steps.description: Add palm oil, crayfish, dried fish and stock cubes, mashing some plantain to thicken.

steps.heading: Greens
steps.description: Stir in the ugu and turn off the heat.

name: Asaro (Yam Porridge)
whatMakesItGood: Asaro is meant to be mashed, not left in neat cubes. Break the yam down against the pot so it becomes one thick porridge.
description: Yam mashed into its own peppery, palm-oiled sauce until it is thick and orange.

steps.heading: Boil the yam
steps.description: Peel, cube and boil the yam with the blended pepper and onion until very soft.

steps.heading: Mash
steps.description: Break the yam down against the side of the pot until it thickens into a porridge.

steps.heading: Enrich
steps.description: Stir in the palm oil, crayfish, dried fish and stock cubes.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Simmer a few more minutes and salt to taste.

name: Basic Tomato Stew Base
whatMakesItGood: Made once and portioned, this is the thing that turns a forty-minute dinner into a ten-minute one. It freezes for months.
description: The fried pepper base with no meat in it — made in bulk and frozen for the week.

steps.heading: Blend
steps.description: Blend the tomatoes, tatashe, scotch bonnet and two onions until smooth.

steps.heading: Reduce
steps.description: Boil the blend in a dry pot until almost all the water has gone.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Fry the reduced blend in hot oil with the sliced onion and tomato paste until the oil floats clear on top.

steps.heading: Cool and store
steps.description: Season, cool completely, and portion into containers to freeze.

name: Obe Ata Dindin
whatMakesItGood: Leaving the tomato out is the whole point. Without its sweetness and water the pepper stays forward and the stew keeps far longer.
description: Fried pepper stew with no tomato at all — hotter, redder and sharper than the usual base.

steps.heading: Blend
steps.description: Blend the tatashe, scotch bonnet and one onion coarsely.

steps.heading: Reduce
steps.description: Boil the blend down in a dry pot until thick.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Fry in hot oil with sliced onion until it darkens and the oil separates completely.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Add crayfish, stock cubes and salt, and cook two minutes more.

name: Coconut Rice
whatMakesItGood: Different from coconut jollof: there is no tomato here at all. Salt it properly, because coconut milk flattens seasoning.
description: White rice cooked in coconut milk with vegetables — no pepper base, so the coconut carries it.

steps.heading: Wash the rice
steps.description: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.

steps.heading: Start the pot
steps.description: Fry the onion in oil, then pour in the coconut milk with stock cubes and salt.

steps.heading: Cook
steps.description: Add the rice, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest heat until the liquid is gone.

steps.heading: Vegetables
steps.description: Fold the diced carrot and beans through near the end and steam covered.

name: Chicken Stew
whatMakesItGood: Fry the chicken first and use its stock in the sauce. Boiling chicken directly in stew makes the sauce watery and the meat bland.
description: Fried chicken simmered in the pepper base until the sauce clings to every piece.

steps.heading: Season and boil
steps.description: Boil the chicken with onion, curry, thyme and stock cubes in little water. Keep the stock.

steps.heading: Fry the chicken
steps.description: Drain and fry the pieces until golden, then set aside.

steps.heading: Reduce the blend
steps.description: Blend and boil down the tomatoes, tatashe, pepper and onion until dry.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Fry in the oil with the tomato paste until the oil separates.

steps.heading: Combine
steps.description: Return the chicken with the stock and simmer until thick.

name: Suya Wrap
whatMakesItGood: Built for leftover suya. Warm the bread first so it folds without cracking, and keep the sauce thick or it soaks through.
description: Leftover suya rolled into flatbread with onion, cabbage and pepper sauce.

steps.heading: Warm the bread
steps.description: Heat the flatbread in a dry pan until soft and pliable.

steps.heading: Prep the filling
steps.description: Shred the cabbage and slice the onion thinly.

steps.heading: Assemble
steps.description: Lay the suya down the middle, top with cabbage, onion and a dusting of dry pepper.

steps.heading: Roll
steps.description: Fold in the ends and roll tightly, then cut in half.

name: Fish Stew
whatMakesItGood: Fish goes in last and is never stirred. Add it early and you get a stew with fish debris in it rather than pieces of fish.
description: Fried fish laid into the pepper base at the very end so it holds together.

steps.heading: Season and fry the fish
steps.description: Season the fish, dry it, and fry until the skin is firm. Set aside carefully.

steps.heading: Reduce the blend
steps.description: Blend and boil down the tomatoes, peppers and onion until the water is gone.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Fry in the oil with the paste until the oil rises clear.

steps.heading: Add the fish
steps.description: Lay the fish in, spoon sauce over it, and simmer without stirring.

name: Peppered Snail
whatMakesItGood: Cleaning is the whole job — lime or alum and repeated rinsing is what takes the slime off. Skip it and no amount of pepper will save the dish.
description: Snails cleaned with lime, boiled, then tossed in a thick pepper sauce.

steps.heading: Clean the snails
steps.description: Wash with lime and salt, rubbing hard and rinsing repeatedly until no slime is left.

steps.heading: Boil
steps.description: Cook with onion, stock cubes and salt until tender.

steps.heading: Make the sauce
steps.description: Blend and fry the peppers and onion in oil until thick and the oil separates.

steps.heading: Toss
steps.description: Fold the drained snails through the sauce and cook two minutes more.

name: Kunu Zaki
whatMakesItGood: A portion of the grain is cooked and blended back in — that is what thickens it and stops it separating in the glass.
description: Millet drink spiced with ginger and cloves, lightly fermented and served cold.

steps.heading: Soak
steps.description: Soak the millet overnight with the ginger and cloves.

steps.heading: Blend
steps.description: Blend everything smooth with some of the water.

steps.heading: Cook part
steps.description: Take a third of the blend and cook it into a thin pap, then stir it back into the raw portion.

steps.heading: Sieve and chill
steps.description: Strain, sweeten to taste, and chill thoroughly.

name: Ofe Owerri
whatMakesItGood: Traditionally the soup you cook when money is not the constraint. Three different leaves and no water added beyond the stock is what makes it Owerri rather than ordinary.
description: The expensive one — uziza, ugu and okazi together with cocoyam thickener and a lot of assorted meat.

steps.heading: Cook the meats
steps.description: Boil the beef, stockfish and ponmo with stock cubes until tender. Reduce the stock — this soup is never watery.

steps.heading: Cocoyam paste
steps.description: Boil the cocoyam until soft and pound it completely smooth.

steps.heading: Thicken
steps.description: Drop the paste into the boiling stock in lumps, cover, and let it dissolve before stirring.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Add palm oil, crayfish, ground pepper and dried fish, and simmer until it thickens properly.

steps.heading: The leaves
steps.description: Add the okazi first, then the ugu and uziza, and turn off after three minutes.

name: Banga Rice
whatMakesItGood: The rice cooks in the palm extract itself rather than in stock, so it takes the colour and the scent all the way through.
description: Rice cooked directly in palm fruit concentrate with banga spices — deep orange and heavily scented.

steps.heading: Parboil
steps.description: Parboil the rice briefly and rinse it well.

steps.heading: Reduce the palm
steps.description: Boil the palm concentrate with onion, pepper and crayfish until it thickens and the oil rises.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Add the dried fish and stock cubes and taste it — the liquid should be strongly seasoned before the rice goes in.

steps.heading: Cook
steps.description: Stir the rice in, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest heat until absorbed.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Fold the scent leaf through and rest it covered for five minutes.

name: Garden Egg Sauce
whatMakesItGood: Boil the garden eggs first and mash them rather than frying them raw — that is what takes the bitterness down to a pleasant background note.
description: Garden eggs boiled soft and mashed into a palm oil and pepper sauce, eaten with yam or plantain.

steps.heading: Boil
steps.description: Boil the garden eggs until completely soft, then peel and mash them.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Fry the blended pepper and onion in palm oil until the oil separates.

steps.heading: Combine
steps.description: Stir the mashed garden egg in with crayfish, dried fish and stock cubes.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Simmer until thick and check the salt.

name: Goat Meat Pepper Soup
whatMakesItGood: Goat carries pepper soup better than any other meat because the fat melts into the broth. Let it simmer long and skim the top as it goes.
description: Goat simmered in a clear, fiercely spiced broth — the bar order and the cold-weather cure.

steps.heading: Sweat the goat
steps.description: Put the goat in a dry pot with onion, ginger and stock cubes and let it sweat before any water goes in.

steps.heading: Simmer
steps.description: Add water to cover and simmer until the meat is tender, skimming the surface as it cooks.

steps.heading: Spice it
steps.description: Stir in the pepper soup spice, ground scotch bonnet and uda, and cook on so the spice opens up.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Add scent leaf, check the salt, and serve very hot.

name: Jollof Beans
whatMakesItGood: The beans must be nearly soft before the tomato goes in. Acid stops beans softening, so an early tomato means beans that never cook.
description: Beans cooked in the tomato stew base instead of plain water — red, seasoned and a change from porridge.

steps.heading: Boil the beans
steps.description: Cook the beans in unsalted water until almost soft, topping up with hot water.

steps.heading: Make the base
steps.description: Blend, reduce and fry the tomatoes, peppers and onion with the paste until the oil separates.

steps.heading: Combine
steps.description: Stir the base into the beans and simmer together so the beans take the colour.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Season, mash slightly for body, and salt to taste.

name: Nigerian Breakfast Eggs
whatMakesItGood: Cook the sausage and vegetables first and let the pan cool a moment before the eggs go in, so they set soft instead of browning.
description: Eggs scrambled with sausage, onion and pepper — the hotel breakfast, made at home.

steps.heading: Fry the sausage
steps.description: Slice and fry the sausage until browned at the edges.

steps.heading: Add vegetables
steps.description: Add the onion, tomato and pepper and cook until softened.

steps.heading: Add the eggs
steps.description: Beat the eggs, lower the heat, and fold them through slowly.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Take them off while still glossy — they finish cooking in the pan.

name: Yam Balls
whatMakesItGood: The mash must be stiff and fully cooled before shaping. Warm mash will not hold and the balls burst open in the oil.
description: Mashed yam seasoned, rolled around a little filling, crumbed and fried.

steps.heading: Boil and mash
steps.description: Boil the yam in salted water until soft, then mash it smooth with no lumps.

steps.heading: Season and cool
steps.description: Mix in the chopped onion, pepper and stock cubes, then let it cool completely.

steps.heading: Shape
steps.description: Roll into balls, dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Fry in hot oil until evenly golden, turning as they go.

name: Ogi (Fermented Corn Pap)
whatMakesItGood: Ogi is sour because it is fermented, and that is the point. Boiling water poured hard onto a cold slurry is the only way to get it lump-free.
description: Fermented corn starch cooked into a smooth sour pap, taken with milk or with akara.

steps.heading: Make the slurry
steps.description: Mix the ogi with cold water until completely smooth.

steps.heading: Pour boiling water
steps.description: Pour freshly boiled water in fast while stirring hard, until it thickens and turns translucent.

steps.heading: Adjust
steps.description: If it is too thick, loosen with a little more boiling water — never cold.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Sweeten and add milk to taste.

name: Efo Riro
whatMakesItGood: The vegetable goes in last and barely cooks. Efo riro is a stew that happens to have spinach in it, not boiled greens.
description: Spinach stewed in a fried pepper base with iru, assorted meat and plenty of palm oil.

steps.heading: Cook the meats
steps.description: Boil the beef and ponmo with stock cubes and onion until tender, keeping the stock.

steps.heading: Wash the greens
steps.description: Wash and slice the shoko, then squeeze out as much water as you can.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Blend the peppers and onion coarsely and fry in palm oil until the oil separates.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Add the iru, crayfish, dried fish, meats and a little stock, and simmer.

steps.heading: Greens last
steps.description: Stir the shoko in, cook two minutes, and take it off the heat.
